questions.stem: What does Snowflake Time Travel enable?

options.text: Accessing historical data that has been changed or deleted within a defined period
Replicating data to another region automatically
Encrypting data at rest with customer-managed keys
Compressing micro-partitions to reduce storage

explanation.correct: Time Travel enables accessing historical data (data changed or deleted) at any point within a defined retention period, supporting querying, cloning, and restoring past data.

distractors.B: Cross-region replication is a separate feature, not Time Travel.
distractors.C: Encryption with customer-managed keys is Tri-Secret Secure, not Time Travel.
distractors.D: Micro-partition compression is unrelated to Time Travel.

questions.stem: What is the standard (default) Time Travel data retention period for all Snowflake accounts?

options.text: 0 days
1 day (24 hours)
7 days
90 days

explanation.correct: The standard retention period is 1 day (24 hours) and is automatically enabled for all Snowflake accounts.

distractors.A: 0 days effectively deactivates Time Travel; it is not the default.
distractors.C: 7 days is the Fail-safe period, not the default Time Travel retention.
distractors.D: 90 days is the maximum for permanent objects on Enterprise Edition, not the default.

questions.stem: On Snowflake Enterprise Edition (or higher), what is the maximum data retention period for PERMANENT databases, schemas, and tables?

options.text: 1 day
7 days
45 days
90 days

explanation.correct: For Enterprise Edition and higher, permanent databases, schemas, and tables can have a retention period from 0 up to 90 days.

distractors.A: 1 day is the default, not the maximum on Enterprise.
distractors.C: 45 days is not a documented Time Travel maximum.

questions.stem: Which THREE actions can be performed on data within the Time Travel retention period? (Select THREE)

options.text: Query data in the past that has since been updated or deleted
Create clones of tables, schemas, and databases at a past point
Recover data through Snowflake Support after the period ends
Restore (UNDROP) tables, schemas, and databases that were dropped
Automatically replicate data to a secondary account
Permanently encrypt historical partitions

explanation.correct: Within the retention period you can query past data, create clones at/before a past point, and UNDROP (restore) dropped tables, schemas, and databases.

distractors.C: Recovery via Snowflake Support after the period ends is Fail-safe, not Time Travel.
distractors.E: Replication is a separate feature, not a Time Travel action.
distractors.F: Time Travel does not perform encryption of historical partitions.

questions.stem: Which TWO SQL extensions were implemented to support Time Travel? (Select TWO)

options.text: The RESTORE POINT command
The ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT command
The AT | BEFORE clause in SELECT and CREATE ... CLONE
The UNDROP command for tables, schemas, and databases
The FLASHBACK QUERY clause

explanation.correct: Time Travel is supported by the AT | BEFORE clause (in SELECT and CREATE ... CLONE) and the UNDROP command for tables, schemas, databases, accounts, external volumes, and tags.

distractors.A: RESTORE POINT is not a Snowflake Time Travel SQL extension.
distractors.B: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT is transaction control, not a Time Travel extension.
distractors.E: FLASHBACK QUERY is Oracle syntax, not Snowflake.

questions.scenario: A data protection lead documents the recovery window that begins after Time Travel retention ends.
questions.stem: What is the duration of the Snowflake Fail-safe period, and is it configurable?

options.text: 1 day, configurable up to 90 days
7 days, non-configurable
14 days, configurable
0 days by default, configurable per object

explanation.correct: Fail-safe provides a non-configurable 7-day period during which historical data may be recoverable by Snowflake, starting immediately after the Time Travel retention period ends.

distractors.A: 1 day up to 90 days describes Time Travel retention, not Fail-safe.
distractors.C: Fail-safe is 7 days and is not configurable.
distractors.D: Fail-safe is fixed at 7 days and cannot be configured per object.

questions.scenario: A user accidentally deleted critical data 10 days ago; Time Travel retention was 1 day and has long since elapsed.
questions.stem: A user deleted critical data 10 days ago; Time Travel retention was 1 day and has elapsed. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: UNDROP TABLE can still restore it instantly
The data is no longer queryable via AT | BEFORE
Only Snowflake can recover it through Fail-safe on a best-effort basis
Cloning the table at a past timestamp will succeed
The data was permanently and irrecoverably erased at deletion time

explanation.correct: After the Time Travel period ends the data is no longer queryable via AT | BEFORE, and only Snowflake can recover it through Fail-safe on a best-effort basis (last resort).

distractors.A: UNDROP works only within the Time Travel retention period, which has elapsed.
distractors.D: Cloning at a past timestamp is unavailable once retention has ended.
distractors.E: The data is not necessarily permanently erased; Fail-safe may recover it.

questions.scenario: An ACCOUNTADMIN wants to configure the default Time Travel retention period for the entire account.
questions.stem: Which parameter is used?

options.text: MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS
MAX_DATA_EXTENSION_TIME_IN_DAYS
DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS
FAILSAFE_RETENTION_DAYS

explanation.correct: DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS is the object parameter (settable by ACCOUNTADMIN) that sets the default retention period for the account and can be overridden per database, schema, or table.

distractors.A: MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS sets a minimum floor; it does not set the default retention itself.
distractors.B: MAX_DATA_EXTENSION_TIME_IN_DAYS relates to extending retention for streams/tasks dependencies, not the default Time Travel period.
distractors.D: FAILSAFE_RETENTION_DAYS is not a real parameter; Fail-safe is fixed at 7 days.

questions.scenario: An ACCOUNTADMIN sets MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS at the account level while DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS is also set on objects.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements correctly describe the effect? (Select TWO)

options.text: The effective retention for an object is MAX(DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS, MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS)
MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS replaces the DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS value
MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS enforces a minimum retention period for objects
The effective retention is the MIN of the two parameters
MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS disables Time Travel entirely

explanation.correct: MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS enforces a minimum retention floor. The effective minimum retention for an object is MAX(DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS, MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS).

distractors.B: It does NOT alter or replace the DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS value.
distractors.D: The effective period uses MAX, not MIN, of the two values.
distractors.E: It sets a minimum retention; it does not disable Time Travel.

questions.scenario: A developer sets DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 0 on a specific table.
questions.stem: What is the effect on that table?

options.text: It extends Time Travel to the maximum 90 days
It moves the table immediately into Fail-safe
It effectively deactivates Time Travel for the object
It has no effect because 0 is not allowed

explanation.correct: A retention period of 0 days for an object effectively deactivates Time Travel for that object.

distractors.A: Setting 0 does not extend retention; it removes it.
distractors.B: Setting 0 does not immediately move current data to Fail-safe as a configuration action.
distractors.D: 0 is allowed and effectively turns off Time Travel for the object.

questions.scenario: A developer needs to pinpoint a historical point a fixed number of seconds in the past.
questions.stem: Which AT | BEFORE parameter specifies the difference in seconds from the current time?

options.text: TIMESTAMP
OFFSET
STATEMENT
INTERVAL

explanation.correct: OFFSET specifies the difference in seconds from the current time, in the form -N (e.g., -120 for 120 seconds ago).

distractors.A: TIMESTAMP specifies an exact date and time, not a seconds offset.
distractors.C: STATEMENT references a query ID as the reference point.
distractors.D: INTERVAL is not a valid AT | BEFORE parameter.

questions.scenario: A developer uses AT(STATEMENT => '<query_id>') where the referenced query ran 20 days ago.
questions.stem: A developer uses AT(STATEMENT => '<query_id>'). Which TWO statements about the STATEMENT parameter are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Query IDs never expire for Time Travel purposes
It silently falls back to the current time when expired
The query ID must reference a query executed within the last 14 days
If the query is older than 14 days, an error is returned
It automatically converts to an OFFSET when expired

explanation.correct: The STATEMENT query ID must reference a query executed within the last 14 days; if it is older, an error ('statement <query_id> not found') is returned.

distractors.A: Query IDs are limited to the last 14 days for STATEMENT-based Time Travel.
distractors.B: It does not silently fall back to current time; it errors.
distractors.E: It does not auto-convert to an OFFSET.

questions.scenario: A developer queries historical data via Time Travel after the table's columns changed.
questions.stem: Which schema is used to interpret the historical data?

options.text: The schema as it existed at the historical point
A merged schema of past and present
The current table schema
No schema; raw bytes are returned

explanation.correct: When querying historical data in a table or non-materialized view, the current table or view schema is used.

distractors.A: Snowflake uses the current schema, not the historical schema.
distractors.B: There is no merged schema; the current schema applies.
distractors.D: Data is returned per the current schema, not as raw bytes.

questions.stem: Once an object's retention period ends and its historical data moves to Fail-safe, which THREE actions are NO LONGER possible? (Select THREE)

options.text: Ingesting new data into the current table
Creating a new table in the schema
Querying the historical data
Cloning past objects
Restoring past objects that were dropped
Granting privileges on the current table

explanation.correct: After the retention period ends, historical data is no longer available for querying, past objects can no longer be cloned, and dropped past objects can no longer be restored.

distractors.A: Ingesting new data into the current table is unaffected by the historical data moving to Fail-safe.
distractors.B: Creating new tables is a normal operation, unaffected.
distractors.F: Granting privileges on the current object is unaffected.

questions.scenario: A DBA reviews the retention rules for different table types on Standard vs Enterprise Edition.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about retention limits are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Transient and temporary tables can have retention up to 90 days on Enterprise
On Standard Edition, retention can be set to 0 or the default of 1 day
Permanent tables on Standard can be set up to 90 days
On Enterprise, transient and temporary tables can have retention of 0 or 1 day
Temporary tables always retain data for 7 days

explanation.correct: On Standard Edition, retention can be 0 or the 1-day default. On Enterprise, transient and temporary tables can be set to 0 or 1 day (only permanent objects support up to 90 days).

distractors.A: Transient and temporary tables cannot use 90-day retention; that applies to permanent objects.
distractors.C: Standard Edition does not support up to 90 days; that requires Enterprise or higher.
distractors.E: Temporary tables do not have a fixed 7-day retention; 7 days is the Fail-safe period.

questions.scenario: A team estimates how long recovering data through Fail-safe might take during an emergency.
questions.stem: What is the expected recovery time and nature of Fail-safe?

options.text: Instant, self-service recovery by the user
Guaranteed within 1 hour by Snowflake Support
Not possible; Fail-safe is only for billing metrics
Several hours to several days, performed by Snowflake on a best-effort basis

explanation.correct: Data recovery through Fail-safe may take from several hours to several days and is provided by Snowflake on a best-effort basis, intended only when all other recovery options have been attempted.

distractors.A: Fail-safe is not self-service or instant; only Snowflake can recover the data.
distractors.B: There is no 1-hour guarantee; recovery can take hours to days.
distractors.C: Fail-safe is a real data recovery service, not just a billing metric.

questions.scenario: An ACCOUNTADMIN wants to view how much data is stored in Fail-safe for the account.
questions.stem: Where in Snowsight can this be viewed?

options.text: Admin » Cost management » Consumption, filtered by Storage usage type
Data » Databases » Fail-safe tab
Worksheets » Query history
Admin » Users & Roles

explanation.correct: Using the ACCOUNTADMIN role in Snowsight, go to Admin » Cost management » Consumption, filter by the Storage usage type, and review the Storage Breakdown for Fail-safe storage.

distractors.B: There is no Fail-safe tab under Data » Databases for this metric.
distractors.C: Query history does not show Fail-safe storage totals.
distractors.D: Users & Roles manages access, not storage consumption.

questions.scenario: A team runs a long-running Time Travel query on a large table near the end of its retention period.
questions.stem: What effect does this have on data moving into Fail-safe?

options.text: It immediately forces the data into Fail-safe
It permanently extends the Time Travel period
It has no effect on Fail-safe timing
It delays moving data and objects into Fail-safe until the query completes

explanation.correct: A long-running Time Travel query delays moving any data and objects (tables, schemas, and databases) in the account into Fail-safe until the query completes.

distractors.A: It delays, rather than forces, the move into Fail-safe.
distractors.B: It does not permanently extend the retention period.
distractors.C: It does affect timing by delaying the move until the query finishes.

questions.scenario: A cost analyst reviews how Fail-safe is billed and its limitations.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about Fail-safe billing and limitations are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Fail-safe recovery is free of any compute charges
Fail-safe storage is never billed
Fail-safe can be used for routine access to historical data
Fail-safe data recovery uses Snowflake-managed serverless compute with standard serverless billing
Fail-safe does not support tables containing data ingested by Snowpipe Streaming Classic

explanation.correct: Fail-safe recovery uses Snowflake-managed serverless compute (standard serverless billing, FAILSAFE_RECOVERY service type), and it does not support tables containing data ingested by Snowpipe Streaming Classic.

distractors.A: Recovery incurs standard serverless compute charges; it is not free.
distractors.B: Fail-safe storage is billed as part of account storage usage.
distractors.C: Fail-safe is not for routine access to historical data; it is a last-resort recovery service used only by Snowflake.

questions.scenario: An ACCOUNTADMIN sets DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 0 at the account level.
questions.stem: What is the effect, and can it be overridden?

options.text: All new databases/schemas/tables default to no retention, but this can be overridden per object at any time
Time Travel is permanently disabled for the entire account and cannot be overridden
It forces a 90-day retention on all objects
It deletes all existing objects in the account

explanation.correct: Setting DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 0 at the account level means all databases (and their schemas/tables) default to no retention, but this default can be overridden at any time for any database, schema, or table. Time Travel cannot be deactivated for an account.

distractors.B: Time Travel cannot be fully deactivated for an account, and object-level overrides are allowed.
distractors.C: Setting 0 removes default retention; it does not force 90 days.
distractors.D: It does not delete existing objects.
